extracted.intended_audience: educational psychologists, researchers of self-regulated learning, graduate students in educational psychology
extracted.subtask_description: A scholarly review comparing major self-regulated learning (SRL) theoretical models and their measurement, synthesizing model components, empirical support, instruments, and research directions. Useful for researchers selecting models, designing SRL studies, or developing interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core components of SRL
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-regulated learning (SRL) includes the cognitive, metacognitive, behavioral, motivational, and emotional/affective aspects of learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the broad domain that SRL models must address; used as an umbrella for variables such as self-efficacy, volition, and cognitive strategies. (Intro)

rubrics_metrics.name: Model inclusion criteria (selection for review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Models included must be: (a) published in JCR journals or SRL handbooks (peer-reviewed); (b) written in English; (c) have a minimum number of citations (models published earlier than 2010: ≥500 references; models published after 2010: ≥20 cites/year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used by the author to decide which SRL models to analyze; shows how to operationalize 'consolidated theoretical and empirical background'. (Methods: Criteria for Inclusion)

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical support / validation
rubrics_metrics.description: A model should have empirical evidence supporting its constructs and processes (e.g., experimental, longitudinal, training studies, meta-analyses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author examines empirical work (microanalytic studies, training studies, meta-analyses) for each model; empirical support is a primary axis of comparison and validation (see sections on each model's empirical evidence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Citations / scholarly impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of citations and the model's uptake in the literature as an indicator of influence and consolidation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a quantitative proxy for a model's prominence and continued use; cited explicitly as one of the comparison aspects. (Abstract, Methods)

rubrics_metrics.name: Phases and subprocesses (model granularity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the model specifies temporal phases of SRL and the subprocesses belonging to each phase (e.g., forethought/analysis, goal setting, planning, monitoring, control, reflection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparative criterion across models — e.g., Zimmerman (forethought, performance, self-reflection), Pintrich (forethought, monitoring, control, reaction), Winne (four linked phases). The presence and definition of subprocesses matter for measurement and intervention design.

rubrics_metrics.name: How (meta)cognition, motivation, and emotion are conceptualized
rubrics_metrics.description: How each model defines and integrates metacognitive processes, motivational beliefs/strategies, and emotional/affective regulation within SRL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Models differ (Pintrich emphasizes motivation; Boekaerts highlights emotion and appraisal; Winne focuses on metacognition). Important for choosing measures and designing interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top–down / bottom–up processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether and how the model accounts for top–down (goal-driven, mastery-focused) versus bottom–up (emotion/need-driven, well-being-focused) regulatory processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boekaerts' Dual Processing model explicitly frames two pathways; Efklides offers a different interpretation. This distinction affects predicted strategies and interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automaticity
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition of automatic vs. controlled processes in SRL (the role of automaticity in regulation and skill execution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included as a comparative dimension; affects how models explain skill development and when interventions need to target conscious strategies versus automatic behaviors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual factors
rubrics_metrics.description: The role of task, environment, time, social context and other conditions in shaping SRL processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Winne's COPES 'Conditions' facet and Pintrich's 'context' area exemplify the need to model situational constraints; context influences measurement and generalizability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards, criteria and self-assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: The presence of explicit standards/criteria that learners use to monitor and evaluate their products (self-assessment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Winne emphasizes use of standards and evaluations; aligns SRL with self-assessment research (e.g., Andrade). Important for operationalizing monitoring and evaluation processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zimmerman — Cyclical Phases model (forethought, performance, self-reflection)
rubrics_metrics.description: SRL organized into three phases: forethought (task analysis, goal setting, planning, motivational beliefs), performance (executing the task, monitoring, self-control strategies), and self-reflection (attributions, self-reactions affecting future approaches).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a foundational, socio-cognitive cyclic structure for interventions and measurement; empirical studies (e.g., sport and academic tasks) support phase-focused training effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zimmerman — Multi-level model (developmental stages of SRL)
rubrics_metrics.description: A multi-level account describing stages by which learners acquire self-regulatory competence (developmental progression).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides expectations about how SRL skills change with expertise and informs design of phase-specific training (e.g., process goals to outcome goals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Boekaerts — Six-component structural model
rubrics_metrics.description: Six components: (1) domain-specific knowledge and skills, (2) cognitive strategies, (3) cognitive self-regulatory strategies, (4) motivational beliefs and theory of mind, (5) self-regulatory motivation strategies, (6) motivational strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A structural taxonomy for analyzing domain-specific SRL elements and for instrument/intervention design (Boekaerts, 1996b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Boekaerts — Dual Processing / Adaptable Learning model (mastery vs well-being pathways)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two parallel processing modes (mastery/learning mode vs coping/well-being mode), driven by appraisals that activate goal pathways; three purposes of self-regulation: (a) expanding knowledge/skills, (b) preventing threat to the self and loss of resources, (c) protecting commitments by redirecting from well-being to mastery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes appraisal, emotion regulation, volitional strategies, and the dynamic shift between pathways; important for diagnosing why learners disengage or avoid tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Winne & Hadwin — Four-phase model and COPES framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Four recursive phases: (a) task definition, (b) goal setting and planning, (c) enacting study tactics/strategies, (d) metacognitively adapting studying. COPES facets: Conditions, Operations (SMART: Searching, Monitoring, Assembling, Rehearsing, Translating), Products, Evaluations, Standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a fine-grained metacognitive/information-processing account; COPES is used to analyze task facets and to derive trace-based measures in computer-supported settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pintrich — Four phases and four regulation areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Phases: (1) Forethought/planning/activation, (2) Monitoring, (3) Control, (4) Reaction and reflection. Areas for regulation: cognition, motivation/affect, behavior, and context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrates motivation and context explicitly with cognition and behavior; MSLQ originates from this theoretical base and supports questionnaire-based measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efklides — interaction of emotion, motivation and metacognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Model exploring how emotion and motivation interact with metacognition and providing a different interpretation of top–down/bottom–up processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights affective-cognitive interactions at micro-levels and guides measures sensitive to momentary emotion-metacognition coupling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hadwin, Järvelä & Miller — Socially Shared Regulation (SSRL)
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasis on the social aspects of regulation in collaborative learning: shared planning, monitoring, and regulation across group members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extends SRL to collaborative/CSCL contexts; measurement requires temporal-sequence analysis of interaction (e.g., chat logs) and design of CSCL regulation tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation of motivation as an explicit SRL dimension
rubrics_metrics.description: Attention to how learners regulate their motivational states (strategies to maintain/increase motivation), an area noted as underemphasized but essential (Wolters, 2003).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Models and measurement approaches should incorporate motivational regulation processes and connect them with cognitive/metacognitive regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of emotions and emotion-regulation strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Emotions (prospective, anticipatory, during-task) and emotion-regulation strategies influence pathway selection (mastery vs well-being) and outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boekaerts' work and OMQ studies illustrate measuring momentary emotions and their effect; gender differences and predictive relations with effort and performance are noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement instruments (questionnaires/scales)
rubrics_metrics.description: Established instruments referenced: SRLIS (Self-Regulated Learning Interview Schedule), MSLQ (Motivated Strategies for Learning Questionnaire), OMQ (Online Motivation Questionnaire), A-SRL (Academic Self-Regulation Scale), LASSI, SELF (Self-Efficacy for Learning Form), Confidence and Doubt scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These instruments are used to operationalize SRL components across models; authors discuss validation, convergent evidence, and limits of questionnaire approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement methods (microanalytic, trace data, diaries, neural networks, computer scaffolding)
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods include microanalytic on-the-fly measures, trace/log data from computer environments (gStudy/nStudy), learning diaries with time-series analysis, neural network predictive models, and experimental training protocols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author highlights a 'third wave' of SRL measurement where intervention and measurement are combined; each method suits different model facets (e.g., trace data for COPES, diaries for temporal dynamics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervention/training effects and dosage (phase-based training)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence that training covering more SRL phases leads to better performance (Cleary et al. studies showed linear trend: more phases trained → better scores); learning diaries enhance SRL phases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as an evaluation criterion for model utility: whether model-derived training produces measurable performance gains and which components/phases are most amenable to instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differential effects by developmental stage / educational level
rubrics_metrics.description: SRL models and interventions may have differential effects depending on students' developmental stage, expertise level, or educational setting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review concludes models show variable effects across developmental stages; researchers and teachers should apply differential effects in practice and design age-appropriate interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of data mining / learning analytics
rubrics_metrics.description: Applying educational data mining, neural networks, and learning analytics to model/tracing SRL processes and to predict performance or SRL profiles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Winne and colleagues, and Boekaerts' collaborations, demonstrate high predictive power using neural networks and trace analysis; recommended as a modern measurement and research approach.
